<teammate-message teammate_id="review-3005-codegen-closure" color="pink" summary="Decision: implemented #3005, PR #3013, CI running">
Decision: IMPLEMENT (worth pre-v1). #3005 is a real generator-shape gap — the concept-read codegen (#2899) exists to eliminate hand-patching, and Android's guarded `AppHandle::with_app` accessor was locking a whole platform out of it. Closure-mode design is the right one and matches the issue author's proposal.

PR: #3013 (branch feat/codegen-guarded-closure-3005, off latest origin/master 3b3e48e78).

What I did:
- Added `facade.runtime_accessor_shape` registry field: "ref" (default) | "closure".
- Closure mode emits `self.<accessor>(|app| <concept_fn>(app, ...))`, mapping accessor `None` (dead/inert handle) → OpenFailed on open / false on close (idempotent D6), and keeping the concept door's own error on the same variant ref mode uses per target shape (JSON→OpenFailed, plain-string→InvalidTarget).
- Ref-mode output is byte-identical (early dispatch), so no existing iOS facade drifts. Swift/Kotlin wrappers untouched — signatures identical, only Rust host access changes.
- Generator stays concept-crate-dependency-free: host-type-agnostic, stamps `app` as the door's first arg (symmetric to ref mode's `self.<accessor>()`).
- Tests: both modes + default-is-ref + invalid-shape reject. `cargo test -p nmp-codegen` 159 pass; `cargo test -p nmp-testing --test doctrine_lint_smoke` 210 pass. Rendered closure output verified as valid Rust.
